title: T-20260705-fix-docpath-workflow-gates-review-scope- - Fix DocPath workflow gates, review scope, promote safety, and knowledge extraction quality

included: Workflow gate semantics for `check`, `agent enter`, `changes`, and commit readiness.
Review diff-base semantics for task-level review after intermediate commits.
Safe promote behavior for existing task/spec artifacts.
Closeout guidance for canonical task files and `current` aliases.
Journal/learn extraction filters for seed specs, placeholders, and non-reusable mechanical details.
Automated tests and updated command output expectations.
excluded: Replacing the DocPath workflow model wholesale.
Adding a database, remote service, or network-dependent review/learn system.
Migrating historical task artifacts except where tests need fixtures.

major_change_gate.user_confirmed: User replied `同意` on 2026-07-05 after the major-change direction was summarized.
major_change_gate.decision_brief_markdown:
- 当前问题: DocPath treats several lifecycle gates as if there is only one valid execution context: clean worktree, active task, and uncommitted local diffs. Real usage has shaping/promoting work before a task exists, step-level commits during a task, and closeout evidence after changes already exist. Generated seed content can also overwrite or pollute durable artifacts.
- 目标: Make DocPath lifecycle gates composable across intake, task execution, and closeout while protecting user-authored artifacts and keeping durable knowledge extraction trustworthy.
- 背景: User reported and confirmed the five defects on 2026-07-05.
- 可选方案:
  - 方案 A: Patch each symptom independently.
  - 方案 B: Define explicit command contexts and evidence ownership rules, then implement targeted fixes in each affected command.
  - 方案 C: Suspend strict gates when conflicts occur.
- 推荐方案: 方案 B
- 决策理由: Explicit contexts make the behavior testable and reduce future contradictions without weakening gates. Option A risks repeated local exceptions. Option C would make DocPath less trustworthy.
- 不做什么: Do not remove standard gates, bypass review/check, or teach agents to ignore DocPath. The framework itself must provide a valid route.
- 成本: Medium to high; likely touches workflow state/routing, check/review/change closeout logic, backlog promotion, journal/learn extraction, and tests.
- 风险: Check could become over-permissive; cumulative review could include unrelated commits if the task base is wrong; promote safety could break existing flows; journal filters could suppress valid lessons if too aggressive.
- 回滚方案: Revert the task commits. Command-level changes should restore previous behavior without data migration.
- 用户确认: User replied `同意` on 2026-07-05 after the major-change direction was summarized.

functional_requirements.text: Resolve the check/agent-enter/dirty-worktree deadlock. `docpath check` must support the valid contexts needed by the workflow, including pre-task/intake review and dirty pre-commit closeout, without requiring an impossible active-task state.
Make `docpath review` capable of reviewing the task cumulative diff, not only the current working-tree diff. A committed step sequence must still be reviewable before task closeout.

Make `docpath backlog promote` safe when target task specs already exist. It must not silently overwrite hand-written specs; it should merge, warn and abort, or preserve a backup with explicit recovery guidance.

Clarify canonical task artifact versus `current` alias behavior in closeout guidance. `docpath changes --agent` and related commit guidance should prefer canonical evidence paths and identify alias files as pointers/views unless they are intentionally required.
Add journal/learn quality gates so seed boilerplate, placeholder options, and mechanical implementation details are not persisted as ADRs or reusable lessons.
Add regression tests for each defect class and for the intended closeout path.

non_functional_requirements.text: Preserve compatibility for normal quick and standard task flows.
Keep all behavior deterministic and locally testable; do not introduce external LLM or network dependencies.
Error messages and `--agent` output must explain the next valid command when a gate blocks progress.
Avoid broad refactors outside the modules that own workflow state, backlog promotion, review/change diff calculation, and journal/learn extraction.

acceptance_criteria.text: A dirty pre-commit worktree with task changes has a valid `docpath check` / `docpath changes --agent` path and no longer requires an impossible `agent enter` transition.
A pre-task or intake/review context can run the appropriate check gate, or receives a precise command-specific explanation that does not deadlock the workflow.
`docpath review` can review cumulative task changes after intermediate commits; tests cover the clean-working-tree-after-commit case.
`docpath backlog promote` refuses, merges, or backs up when an existing user-authored spec would be overwritten; tests cover the data-loss scenario.
`docpath changes --agent` identifies canonical evidence paths versus `current` alias paths and recommends staging canonical artifacts by default.
`journal` / `learn` filters reject seed-spec boilerplate, placeholder option text, and mechanical implementation details; tests cover the examples reported by the user.
Existing quick/standard happy-path tests continue to pass.
The task completes with `docpath check`, `docpath review`, and journal evidence without manual state-file edits.
